name: Dark Aquamarine
lede: Dark Aquamarine is a deep, bluish-green modifier on [[aquamarine]], scanned from Ridgway's 1912 plates and filed by the ISCC-NBS system in 1955.

sections.title: A darker reading of aquamarine
sections.body:
The name follows the library's modifier grammar, *dark* plus [[aquamarine]] [1]. Ridgway's 1912 *Color Standards and Color Nomenclature* places a close hue at plate VII, hue 39, a scan of an aged plate and so only approximate [1]. Our library's nearest computed ISCC-NBS block for this chip is a moderate bluish green, and Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary separately dates a hue this dark to 1912 as well [1].

The books do not explain why "dark" was chosen over another modifier for this reading [2]. Its nearest named neighbors by color distance are [[anthracene-green]] and [[deep-teal-green]], both almost indistinguishable at 3.1 units, with [[myrtle-green]] a little further at 3.5 [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: A color this close to Dark Aquamarine is rare in our archive: 20 of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, about 0.08 percent, rarer than 70 percent of the named colors [4]. The earliest match is a 1520 painting, 392 years before the name's earliest record [4]. That is centuries before the name's own record, a floor on the hue's age, not a first use of either the name or a pigment.
